sentences.text:
By way of filing the present revision petition, the petitioner- accused has challenged the order dated 18.02.2003 passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Pratapgarh in Criminal Regular Case No.219/1991 whereby the learned Magistrate has convicted and sentenced the petitioner for the offences under Sections 7/16 (1) (A) (1)(11) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the order dated 13.12.2004 passed by the learned Additional Session Judge and Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act cases, Pratapgarh in Criminal Appeal No.11/2004 whereby the judgment of the learned trial Court has been upheld.
As per prosecution, on 23.11.1990 milk samples were taken from the petitioner who is in milk vendor.

The report of the milk samples prepared by public analysis inconformity with the procedure provided under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act revealed that the milk found in the possession of the petitioner [2024:RJ-JD:10573] (2 of 4) [CRLR-939/2004] was 'Adulterated'.
The petitioner was thereafter prosecuted for the offences under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that incident in the present case relates to the year 1990.
The petitioner does not have any criminal antecedent.

Learned counsel vehemently submitted that after receiving report of public analysis prosecution sanction from the competent authority in Ramlal vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:10573) on 21 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170365149/
1 conformity with the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was not taken.
There is no positive evidence available on record that the petitioner is guilty of committing the alleged crime.
Merely on the basis of the report of public analysis, it cannot be said that the petitioner had committed the alleged crime or the milk was adulterated.
Learned counsel for the petitioner in the alternative submitted that the occurrence relates to the year 1990 and the petitioner has already served some parts of the sentence awarded to him.
Therefore, the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him.

Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka:
2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623 and a judgment of Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CrilLJ 2582.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment and therefore, the same do not call for any interference in exercise or revisional jurisdiction by this Court.
A perusal of the impugned judgments makes its manifest that the alleged incident happened in the year 1990 and the revision petition is pending before this Court for adjudication since 2004.

The record of the case indicates that petitioner had already undergone detention for some period and since the case is pending before this Court since 2004, the petitioner had suffered both financial hardships and mental agony.

In the opinion of this Court, the alternative prayer made by the counsel for the petitioner that since the petitioner had undergone detention for some period, thus,
without making any interference on merits/conviction, the sentence awarded to the present petitioner may be substituted with the period of sentence already undergone by him, deserves acceptance.

Accordingly, while maintaining the conviction of the petitioner for the offences under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the sentences awarded to him i.e. of one years rigorous imprisonment and a fine or Rs.2000/- are reduced to the period already undergone by him.
The petitioner is on bail.
He need not surrender.
His bail bonds stands discharged accordingly.
All pending applications stands disposed of.
Record of the case be send to the learned Court below forthwith.
Thus, the present revision petition lacks merit and is accordingly dismissed.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 31-himanshu/-
